title: Event framing and outcome-signals mapper for OpenAI ChatCompletions compatibility
creator: Ruth Chen
description: Implement a compatibility layer that maps OpenAI Chat Completions request/response envelopes to Redwood's internal streaming/events model while preserving tool calling and structured-output signals. Goal: allow existing customers who use the OpenAI ChatCompletions API surface to migrate to Redwood with identical semantics for partial streaming, function/tool calls, and JSON/structured outputs, and to provide robust fallbacks when model variants differ.
acceptance_criteria: Requests using OpenAI Chat Completions schema (messages array + top-level fields) are accepted by the compat proxy and converted to Redwood canonical request format without user-visible loss.

Streaming chunks produced by models that emit OpenAI-style delta messages are mapped into Redwood event stream frames, preserving: role tokens, content deltas, tool_call start/arguments, tool_call completion, stop reasons and flags.

Function/tool calling lifecycle (call request, partial args via stream, completed call) is surfaced to Redwood tooling and to caller via a final structured event equivalent to existing Redwood function-call output.
Structured outputs encoded as content (e.g., JSON blocks or special function outputs) are detected and emitted as structured output events rather than raw text when possible.

Automated test harness verifies parity with a reference OpenAI-compatible implementation for a representative set of streaming scenarios (normal completion, tool call, truncated stream, error mid-stream).
Backward-compatibility: non-streaming usages continue to work and error messages match expected OpenAI semantics (400/422 shapes).
technical_notes: We will implement a small state machine per-connection to track 'openai' stream tokens: role set -> content deltas -> tool_call.start -> tool_call.args (streamed) -> tool_call.end -> finish signals.

Map OpenAI 'assistant' role and delta messages to Redwood 'token' events with metadata: chunk_index, cumulative_length, source_role. Preserve 'finish_reason' mapping (e.g., 'stop'|'length'|'content_filter').

When a tool/function call is initiated (OpenAI uses 'function_call' field), accept both immediate full-arg forms and streamed arg fragments. Buffer streamed args under a size threshold; emit partial arg events for observability and tracing.

For structured outputs, attempt to detect top-level JSON blocks using a tolerant parser (recoverable on trailing partial tokens). If valid, emit as structured_output event with schema: {type: 'json', payload: string}. If parse fails, fall back to text output and add a 'structured_parse_failed' tag.
Expose a compatibility flag on the request (query param or header) to enable strict vs lenient mapping. Default to lenient to maximize compatibility.
Performance: avoid copying large token payloads. Use zero-copy where underlying buffer permits; prefer incremental streaming to avoid O(seq_len) buffering on the proxy path.
implementation_plan: Design: finalize event envelope mapping and state machine (2d). See design doc link in links.
Prototype: implement the mapping layer as a middleware in the request ingress path with feature flag 'openai-cc-compat' (3d).
Integration: wire tool-call lifecycle into Redwood tool-router and ensure tool results are marshalled back to OpenAI response shape when compat flag present (3d).
Testing: add unit tests for the state transitions and end-to-end integration tests using a mock model that emits OpenAI-style streams (2d).
Rollout: behind feature-flag; enable for small subset of customers and run parity traffic for two weeks before gradual ramp.
testing_strategy: Unit tests: state machine transitions covering role->content->tool_call->finish and abnormal terminations.

Integration tests: synthetic model that yields: (1) complete non-streamed response; (2) streaming text deltas; (3) tool call with streamed args; (4) mid-stream error and truncated arg; (5) structured JSON emitted across multiple deltas.
Fuzz tests: random fragmentation of JSON-structured outputs to validate tolerant parser correctness and graceful degradation.
Benchmark: measure additional latency introduced by compat middleware at p50/p95 for small (<=32 token) and long (>1024 token) responses.
User-facing regression tests: run existing OpenAI-compatible examples in the docs and verify byte-for-byte where expected for canonical examples.
